breaking.headline: Trump vows to work with Democrats to cap credit card rates at 10%
breaking.fact: President Trump said Saturday he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, reviving a 2024 campaign pledge that stalled under Republican control. The median card rate is roughly 22.2%, and researchers estimate a 10% cap would save Americans about $100 billion a year in interest; Sen. Elizabeth Warren, expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, replied: 'Let's cap credit card interest rates and save Americans money.' Nothing is law yet - Congress would have to pass it after Democrats take control in January.

breaking.headline: Sanctioned Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Baltic after suspected drone strike
breaking.fact: The Russian-flagged Sparta II, a sanctioned vessel linked to a Russian military logistics firm, caught fire Saturday after being hit by two suspected Ukrainian drones in the Gulf of Finland while bound for Kaliningrad. All 16 crew were evacuated, the fire was still burning into the night, and the ship drifted into Finnish waters; hours later a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating Finnish airspace near Loviisa.

weekInBrief.headline: Senate passes bipartisan permitting bill, 62-33
weekInBrief.body: The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on Thursday, a sweeping rewrite of permitting rules meant to speed up power plants, transmission lines and pipelines and make data centers pay their own energy costs. The bill splits green groups - some back faster clean-energy buildout, others warn it weakens environmental and tribal protections - and now heads to a House out of session for Thanksgiving.

weekInBrief.headline: Mexico captures 'Chapo Isidro,' an FBI Top 10 fugitive
weekInBrief.body: Mexican special forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro,' in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday night, with U.S. intelligence support, touching off gun battles that killed at least 11 people, including four soldiers. The 44-year-old, wanted for trafficking heroin, meth, cocaine and fentanyl into the U.S., carried a $5 million FBI reward and was flown to Mexico City with two other cartel leaders.

weekInBrief.headline: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' sets a $3.79 billion first-day record
weekInBrief.body: Rockstar Games said Friday that GTA VI took in a record $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, the biggest entertainment launch ever, after selling 32.5 million copies before release. The haul dwarfs the $800 million first day of 2013's GTA V and sent parent Take-Two's shares higher.

weekInBrief.headline: Denmark expels Russian defence attache over rapper assassination plot
weekInBrief.body: Denmark said Friday it will expel Russia's defence attache within seven days after its security service said Russian intelligence plotted to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner before a Sept. 25 concert near Copenhagen, recruiting members of the banned gang Loyal to Familia. Danish police stopped three men with guns and knives minutes before the show; Russia denied any involvement.

weekendStories.headline: Volunteers to deliver Thanksgiving meals to homebound Houston seniors
weekendStories.body: Northwest Assistance Ministries is sending volunteers out on Thanksgiving morning, Nov. 26, to deliver holiday meals and a friendly visit to homebound seniors and neighbors with disabilities across northwest Houston. The two-hour commitment, starting at 8 a.m. at the ministry's Kuykendahl Road headquarters, lets volunteers be home for their own celebrations by late morning.

weekendStories.headline: HTX Basket Brigade packs 300 Thanksgiving baskets in one evening
weekendStories.body: Houston neighbors gathered at the Houston Texans YMCA on Nov. 18 to pack 300 Thanksgiving baskets - turkey and all the fixings - for local families, with help from the University of Houston track and field team. The brigade, now its own 501(c)(3) charity, says a $19.79 gift covers a full Thanksgiving meal for one family.

weekendStories.headline: City Wide Club's 48th Super Feast feeds tens of thousands
weekendStories.body: The City Wide Club's Thanksgiving Super Feast returns to the George R. Brown Convention Center this week, serving hot meals, groceries, clothing and household essentials to tens of thousands of Houstonians in one of the nation's largest holiday feeding events. Volunteers can still sign up for Wednesday kitchen prep or one of three Thanksgiving Day shifts.

weekendStories.headline: Plains first-grader wins Sanders County coloring contest
weekendStories.body: Plains first-grader Mya Aquino took first place in the Sanders County Red Ribbon Week Coloring Contest, her artwork standing out among hundreds of entries from kindergarten through third grade across the county. Health department and Elks Lodge volunteers presented her with a gift basket in her classroom - and handed out backpacks to her classmates, too.

weekendStories.headline: Pride of Dakota Holiday Showcase fills Fargo with local makers
weekendStories.body: The Pride of Dakota Holiday Showcase runs Friday and Saturday at Scheels Arena in Fargo, with North Dakota-made foods, art, books, jewelry and home goods from local entrepreneurs - plus Santa visits and a free tote bag with any purchase. Admission is free, thanks to the Bank of North Dakota College SAVE Plan.

weekendStories.headline: U.P.'s first European-style Christmas market opens in Ishpeming
weekendStories.body: The Ishpeming Kriskindlmarkt opens Nov. 27 outside The Mather Inn, turning a downtown parking lot into a village of 20-plus decorated wooden huts with holiday lights, Finnish and German food, bonfires, a sledding hill and a kids' craft corner. The first market of its kind in the Upper Peninsula runs Nov. 27-28 and Dec. 4-5, and admission is free.

weekendStories.headline: Firefighters bring a lost Golden Lab home from a Virginia mountainside
weekendStories.body: Archie, a Golden Labrador missing for days, was found stranded and dehydrated on a steep, wooded slope in Virginia's Bent Mountain area. Roanoke County firefighters and animal rescuers reached him, started IV fluids on the spot, and reunited him with his owner — a happy ending powered by a whole community of helpers.

weekendStories.headline: NASA's exoplanet archive adds four new worlds
weekendStories.body: The week's NASA Exoplanet Archive update adds four newly confirmed planets, including RX J0534 b - a rare giant planet orbiting a low-mass star - plus 21 new transmission spectra that let astronomers probe the atmospheres of distant worlds. One earlier candidate, Gl 48 b, was reclassified as a false positive after its discovery paper was withdrawn.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A tanker sailing outbound through the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile Friday about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, catching fire with no casualties reported, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (Warning 214-26); Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the vessel hit a naval mine, a claim not independently verified. Iran has also positioned more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island in a convoy to test the U.S. blockade, with crews assigned and flags raised, according to TankerTrackers and satellite imagery, while U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Thursday that energy flows through the strait were increasing. On oil, the roughly 200,000 barrels transferred Tuesday has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: SpaceX Dragon splashes down packed with science and cargo
space.body: SpaceX's unpiloted Dragon splashed down in the Pacific near Los Angeles on Saturday, closing NASA's 35th commercial resupply mission to the space station. It brought home a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct for vascular-aging research, frozen tumor organoids for cancer studies, and microbial samples to probe antibiotic resistance in space.

space.headline: ALMA catches a dying Sun-like star in its final act
space.body: Astronomers using the ALMA telescope have captured a rare stage in the death of a Sun-like star 12,000 light-years away in Monoceros: a vast gas shell blown off about 6,500 years ago, now half a light-year wide, with an hourglass-shaped nebula forming inside it. The JPL-led team says the shell preserves evidence of the star's last great nuclear pulse — a real-time snapshot of how stars like our Sun end their lives.

space.headline: Fermi's 14-year map closes astronomy's elusive 'MeV gap'
space.body: A new catalog from NASA's Fermi telescope identifies 450 gamma-ray sources in the hard-to-observe 20-200 MeV range, the clearest low-energy gamma-ray view ever, with counterparts found for 377 of them - mostly blazars outside the Milky Way. Sixty appear to be brand-new gamma-ray discoveries, including one mystery source shining across nine orders of magnitude in energy.

space.headline: Codebreaking math finds a hidden pulsar a million times faster
space.body: Using math borrowed from code-breakers, researchers found a pulsar spinning 261 times a second - PSR J1622-7204 - hiding in 15 years of NASA Fermi data, in about 10 hours of computing on a single processor. The old search method had burned the equivalent of 600 years of computing and still missed it; the technique could unlock many more hidden pulsars, including ones in binary systems.

apod.title: The Cat's Head Nebula
apod.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) — NASA Image of the Day
apod.explanation: The James Webb Space Telescope's mid-infrared view of the Cat's Head Nebula, a dust pillar in the Carina Nebula about 7,500 light-years away. Ultraviolet radiation and winds from massive stars sculpted the feline shape - its glowing white eye is likely a young star still embedded in dust - while warm dust and carbon molecules trace intricate structures through the pillar.
